events.title: Septimius Severus defeats Clodius Albinus at Lugdunum
events.description: Near modern Lyon, Severus won a hard-fought battle against his rival for the throne, said to have involved some 300,000 men. Albinus died, leaving Severus sole emperor.
events.html: Near modern Lyon, Severus won a hard-fought battle against his rival for the throne, said to have involved some 300,000 men. Albinus died, leaving Severus sole emperor.

events.title: Nicolaus Copernicus is born in Toruń
events.description: Copernicus's 'On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres', published as he died in 1543, placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the centre. It became a starting point of the Scientific Revolution.
events.html: Copernicus's 'On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres', published as he died in 1543, placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the centre. It became a starting point of the Scientific Revolution.

events.title: Aaron Burr arrested for treason in Alabama
events.description: The former Vice-President was seized near Wakefield, accused of plotting to found an independent nation in the West. He was acquitted that September, but his political career was over.
events.html: The former Vice-President was seized near Wakefield, accused of plotting to found an independent nation in the West. He was acquitted that September, but his political career was over.

events.title: Edison receives a patent for the phonograph
events.description: Edison's tinfoil phonograph was the first machine able to record sound and play it back. Its first words were 'Mary had a little lamb'.
events.html: Edison's tinfoil phonograph was the first machine able to record sound and play it back. Its first words were 'Mary had a little lamb'.

events.title: Allied fleet begins bombarding the Dardanelles forts
events.description: British and French warships opened fire on Ottoman forts guarding the straits, hoping to force a way to Constantinople. The naval effort failed in March, leading to the Gallipoli landings.
events.html: British and French warships opened fire on Ottoman forts guarding the straits, hoping to force a way to Constantinople. The naval effort failed in March, leading to the Gallipoli landings.

events.title: Roosevelt signs Executive Order 9066
events.description: The order allowed the military to exclude people from designated areas, leading to the internment of about 120,000 Japanese Americans. Congress apologised and paid reparations in 1988.
events.html: The order allowed the military to exclude people from designated areas, leading to the internment of about 120,000 Japanese Americans. Congress apologised and paid reparations in 1988.

events.title: US Marines land on Iwo Jima
events.description: The 36-day battle killed nearly 7,000 Americans and almost all of the 21,000 Japanese defenders. Joe Rosenthal's photograph of the flag raising on Mount Suribachi became an icon.
events.html: The 36-day battle killed nearly 7,000 Americans and almost all of the 21,000 Japanese defenders. Joe Rosenthal's photograph of the flag raising on Mount Suribachi became an icon.
